newsitem.title: USA: NATO enlargement to cost up to $35 bn, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: NATO enlargement to cost up to $35 bn, U.S. says.

text.p: The cost of enlarging NATO to bring in former Warsaw Pact members is expected to be between $27 billion and $35 billion up to the year 2009, the Clinton administration estimated on Monday.
Of this, the United States is expected to bear costs of between $1.5 billion and $2 billion, the administration said in a report to Congress.

The 16-nation alliance is due to announce at a July summit in Madrid the names of countries that will be invited to negotiate membership. The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are believed to be leading contenders.

U.S. officials refused to say how many new members their cost estimates budgeted for. The report said only that "a small group of nonspecified Central European countries would join NATO in the first tranche of enlargement".
The report broke down the enlargement costs into three sections:
-- $10-13 billion in new member costs for military restructuring;
-- $8-10 billion for NATO regional reinforcement capabilities;
